description: Reframing gravity as an emergent swarm behavior: each particle follows simple local rules (attract neighbors, avoid collisions) that produce large-scale gravitational clustering. This inverts the usual perspective — instead of deriving behavior from a global force law, we ask: what minimal local rules produce gravity-like dynamics? This connects to artificial life and self-organization theory.
mathematical_formalization: Each agent i follows: a_i = sum_{j in N_i} [w_attract * (r_j - r_i)/|r_j - r_i| - w_repulse * (r_j - r_i)/|r_j - r_i|^3] + noise. With w_attract ~ 1/r and w_repulse ~ 1/r^3, the net effective force is ~1/r^2 at intermediate distances, recovering Newtonian gravity as an emergent phenomenon.
analogical_connections: Chemotaxis in bacteria: cells follow local chemical gradients, producing macroscopic aggregation patterns similar to gravitational collapse
Ant colony optimization: local pheromone rules produce global shortest-path solutions, like local gravity rules produce global orbital dynamics
Market gravity models in economics: retail locations attract customers with a force proportional to size and inversely proportional to distance squared
implementation_hypothesis: Implement agent-based model where each agent senses neighbors within radius R and applies attraction + short-range repulsion. No global force law. Use spatial hashing for neighbor queries. Tune w_attract and w_repulse to produce stable orbiting clusters. Compare emergent dynamics with Newtonian N-body.
experiment_seed: Initialize 1000 agents randomly. Run swarm rules and Newtonian gravity from same initial conditions. Compute: radial density profile, velocity dispersion profile, and power spectrum of density fluctuations. Quantify how closely swarm dynamics matches gravity.
